name: HELM
description: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models is a comprehensive multi-dimensional evaluation framework defining 42 scenarios (covering QA, summarization, dialogue, code, etc.) and 7 metrics: accuracy, calibration, robustness, fairness, bias, toxicity, and efficiency. Rather than a single benchmark, it is a meta-framework that standardizes prompts, scores, and comparisons across diverse existing datasets.
evaluation_method: accuracy, calibration, toxicity score, fairness metrics, efficiency (token usage)
general_score_metric: composite multi-metric profile (no single aggregate score by design)
typical_sota_score: Varies by scenario and metric; top models achieve >90% accuracy on most scenarios
reputation: Gold standard for formal AI audits and governance; published in TMLR 2023; backed by Stanford CRFM; regularly expanded; widely referenced in responsible AI evaluation and policy contexts
notes: A living framework continuously updated with new scenarios and models. Goes beyond accuracy to measure bias, toxicity, calibration, and efficiency — making it the preferred framework for responsible AI evaluation. Online leaderboard at crfm.stanford.edu. Relies on existing datasets; bias and toxicity metrics depend on third-party tools whose own biases can propagate. Added adaptive testing via Item Response Theory (IRT) in 2025.

institutions: Stanford Center for Research on Foundation Models (CRFM)
